Thanks - looping in the SE notes / concrete guidance for the k6 run. Quoting Marissa's plan below for context.

> Marissa: 'We'll create a scoped API key... Aditya will review your k6 script and send a tuned template + ramp recommendations.'

Technical notes / recommendations:
- Endpoint: use the dedicated test endpoint we'll provide (https://test-inference.redwood.com/finwise).
- API key: 'finwise-loadtest' will be created and shared via secure vault; it will not be subject to production routing.
- Rate guidance: your desired sustained 60 RPS, burst to 120 RPS is fine. We recommend a conservative per-key hard-limit of 200 RPS to avoid accidental noisy-neighbor impact.
- Concurrency & VUs (k6): for 60 RPS with average 0.5s response time, target ~40 VUs with the following ramp plan: 10m ramp to 40 VUs, 30m steady, then 10m ramp to 80 VUs for burst window. For your 250 concurrent sessions goal, run a separate scenario that simulates 250 long-lived clients hitting streaming endpoints.
- Streaming tests: use a dedicated streaming scenario that keeps a persistent websocket/HTTP2 stream per VU. Measure first-byte latency and per-token inter-arrival time (target <30ms/token). k6 has websocket support; we've also attached a streaming example in k6-loadtest-template.js.
- Payload sizing: for short completions use ~60 tokens input / 60 tokens output (estimate ~120 tokens total). For long completions use ~300 tokens output. Estimate token counts to help us configure token-based throttles and to validate cost metrics.
- Warmup / prefix cache: run a 15-20 minute warmup that hits the commonly used prefixes to populate KV/prefix caches. This dramatically reduces cold-start variance during the steady-state run.
- Monitoring & alerts: capture 5xx, client error rates, and p95/p99 latencies. We'll provide temporary dashboards and a Slack alert channel for the window.
- IP confirmation: we will confirm allowlist entries once our infra does the provisioning and will share ip-allowlist-confirmation.txt.
